chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice! The people of the mountains — the fat tails of the sheep become heavy in their possession so they cut them off.' He said: 'It is haram.' I said: 'May I be your sacrifice! We use them to light fires.' He said: 'Do you not know that it touches the hand and the clothing, and it is haram?'

key_terms.أَلَيَاتُ الْغَنَمِ: The fat tails of sheep; an alya (plural alayat) is the broad fatty tail found in some sheep breeds common to the region
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Haram — ritually forbidden and legally impermissible under Islamic law
key_terms.يُصِيبُ الْيَدَ وَالثَّوْبَ: Contacts the hand and clothing — indicating the fat renders them ritually impure (najis) as cut from a living animal

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to cut the fat tails of sheep in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential question put to Imam al-Ridha (AS) regarding the practice in mountain communities of cutting off the heavy fat tails (alya) of sheep and using the fat for fuel. The Imam declared this practice haram. When the questioner mentioned that they use the cut tails as fuel, the Imam reinforced the ruling by noting that the fat contaminates the hand and clothing — implying it causes ritual impurity (najasah) as a severed limb from a living animal.
